claim: Synaptotagmin-1 is the primary Ca2+ sensor for synchronous neuronal exocytosis.
source: The primary Ca2+ sensor for synchronous neuronal exocytosis is synaptotagmin-1 (syt-1), a resident protein of synaptic vesicles that consists of a short luminal domain, a transmembrane α-helix and two cytoplasmic C2 domains, referred to as C2A and C2B.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction section of the manuscript.

claim: Synaptotagmin-1 consists of a short luminal domain, a transmembrane α-helix and two cytoplasmic C2 domains (C2A and C2B).
source: The primary Ca2+ sensor for synchronous neuronal exocytosis is synaptotagmin-1 (syt-1), a resident protein of synaptic vesicles that consists of a short luminal domain, a transmembrane α-helix and two cytoplasmic C2 domains, referred to as C2A and C2B.
evidence: This structural description is stated directly in the text.

claim: C2 domains are composed of structurally conserved eight-stranded anti-parallel β-sandwiches of ~130 residues.
source: The C2 domains of syt-1 are composed of structurally conserved eight-stranded anti-parallel β-sandwiches of ~130 residues.
evidence: This structural description is stated directly in the text.

claim: C2 domains contain Ca2+-binding loops at one end of the β-sandwich motif.
source: These domains contain Ca2+-binding loops at one end of the β-sandwich motif.
evidence: This structural feature is stated directly in the text.

claim: Upon Ca2+ binding, the electrostatic surface potential of the C2 domains is altered.
source: Upon Ca2+ binding, the electrostatic surface potential of the C2 domains is altered.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: Ca2+ binding leads to Coulombic attraction towards the head groups of anionic phospholipids.
source: As a result, Coulombic attraction develops towards the head groups of anionic phospholipids, leading to binding of the C2 domains to the membrane associated with completion of the Ca2+ coordination sphere.
evidence: This mechanism is stated directly in the text.

claim: A conserved polybasic lysine patch located on the C2B domain binds to anionic lipid in the absence of Ca2+.
source: Moreover, a conserved polybasic lysine patch located on the C2B domain also binds to anionic lipid in the absence of Ca2+, being particularly attracted to multivalent phosphoinositides (PtdIns) (Jahn and Fasshauer, 2012; Südhof, 2013; Chapman, 2008; Brose et al., 1992; Corbalan-Garcia and Gómez-Fernández, 2014; Südhof, 2012).
evidence: This is stated directly with supporting citations.

claim: The polybasic lysine patch is particularly attracted to multivalent phosphoinositides.
source: Moreover, a conserved polybasic lysine patch located on the C2B domain also binds to anionic lipid in the absence of Ca2+, being particularly attracted to multivalent phosphoinositides (PtdIns) (Jahn and Fasshauer, 2012; Südhof, 2013; Chapman, 2008; Brose et al., 1992; Corbalan-Garcia and Gómez-Fernández, 2014; Südhof, 2012).
evidence: This is stated directly with supporting citations.

claim: The KAKA mutant (K326A and K327A) does not alter the binding of the syt-1 C2AB fragment to vesicles containing PtdSer and/or PtdIns(4,5)P2 according to some studies.
source: For example, recent studies have reported that a double Lys-to-Ala mutation in the polybasic lysine patch (termed the KAKA mutant) does not alter the binding of the syt-1 C2AB fragment to vesicles containing phosphatidylserine (PtdSer) and/or phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PtdIns(4,5)P2) (Radhakrishnan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a citation of previous work showing conflicting results.

claim: The KAKA mutant decreases the binding of the C2AB fragment to vesicles according to other studies.
source: By contrast, the same mutant was reported in other studies to decrease the binding of the C2AB fragment to vesicles (Vrljic et al., 2011), even in the absence of PtdIns (Li et al., 2006), or to almost completely abolish the binding to soluble PtdIns(4,5)P2, in either the absence or the presence of Ca2+ (van den Bogaart et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a citation of previous work showing conflicting results.

claim: Vesicles containing both PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 yield a lower apparent dissociation constant (Kd) than vesicles containing either PtdSer or PtdIns(4,5)P2 alone.
source: However, vesicles containing both PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 yielded a lower apparent dissociation constant (Kd) than vesicles containing either PtdSer or PtdIns(4,5)P2 alone, even when the vesicles had similar charge density (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: No significant difference was observed in the bimolecular association rate constant (kon) in almost all the tested lipid mixtures.
source: Surprisingly, no significant difference was observed in the bimolecular association rate constant (kon) in almost all the tested lipid mixtures (Figure 1e),
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: The decrease in affinity is solely due to a drop in the unimolecular dissociation rate constant (koff).
source: In other words, the decrease in affinity is solely due to a drop in the unimolecular dissociation rate constant (koff) (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: The association rate for binding of the C2AB fragment to the vesicles is diffusion-limited.
source: Thus, under these experimental conditions, the association rate for binding of the C2AB fragment to the vesicles is diffusion-limited and the binding equilibrium is controlled by the off-rate.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The binding equilibrium is controlled by the off-rate.
source: Thus, under these experimental conditions, the association rate for binding of the C2AB fragment to the vesicles is diffusion-limited and the binding equilibrium is controlled by the off-rate.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: EPR spectra from membrane-embedded spin labels are significantly broadened when the C2AB fragment is fully bound to vesicles.
source: Insertion of the spin-labeled side chain R1 (see Figure 2a) into the hydrophobic core of the membrane alters the rotamer sampling and motion of the spin label. As consequence, the EPR spectra from membrane-embedded spin labels are significantly broadened when the C2AB fragment is fully bound to vesicles (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by EPR experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Labels in the Ca2+-binding loops exhibit more motional averaging when bound to bilayers containing 5% PtdIns(4,5)P2 than when bound to vesicles composed of 20% PtdSer.
source: When bound to bilayers containing 5% PtdIns(4,5)P2, labels in the Ca2+-binding loops exhibit more motional averaging than they do when bound to vesicles composed of either 20% PtdSer (Figure 2a) or 10% PtdSer + 2.5% PtdIns(4,5)P2 (data not shown).
evidence: This is supported by EPR experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: More motional averaging suggests a shallower membrane penetration for R1 when bound to bilayers composed of only PtdIns(4,5)P2 rather than PtdIns(4,5)P2 and PtdSer.
source: This suggests a shallower membrane penetration for R1 when bound to bilayers composed of only PtdIns(4,5)P2 rather than PtdIns(4,5)P2 and PtdSer, in agreement with previous results of experiments based on continuous wave power saturation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the EPR data.

claim: R1 sidechains at sites 173, 234, 368 and 304 penetrate the membrane in the presence of PtdSer regardless of whether PtdIns(4,5)P2 is present.
source: As previously reported (Herrick et al., 2006; Kuo et al., 2009), R1 sidechains at sites 173, 234, 368 and 304 penetrate the membrane in the presence of PtdSer regardless of whether PtdIns(4,5)P2 is present, but failed to deeply penetrate the membrane in vesicles containing only PtdIns(4,5)P2.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and previous citations.

claim: R1 sidechains at sites 173, 234, 368 and 304 failed to deeply penetrate the membrane in vesicles containing only PtdIns(4,5)P2.
source: As previously reported (Herrick et al., 2006; Kuo et al., 2009), R1 sidechains at sites 173, 234, 368 and 304 penetrate the membrane in the presence of PtdSer regardless of whether PtdIns(4,5)P2 is present, but failed to deeply penetrate the membrane in vesicles containing only PtdIns(4,5)P2.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and previous citations.

claim: The insertion depth of the Ca2+-binding loops was 4–6 Ångstroms (Å) shallower in membranes composed of PtdIns(4,5)P2 than in membranes containing PtdSer.
source: As shown in Table 1, the insertion depth of the Ca2+-binding loops was 4–6 Ångstroms (Å) shallower in membranes composed of PtdIns(4,5)P2 than in membranes containing PtdSer.
evidence: This is supported by depth measurement data shown in Table 1.

claim: A label in the polybasic patch, 329R1, was closer to the membrane in PtdIns(4,5)P2-containing vesicles than in PtdSer-containing vesicles.
source: By contrast, a label in the polybasic patch, 329R1, was closer to the membrane in PtdIns(4,5)P2-containing vesicles than in PtdSer-containing vesicles, indicating that there is a difference in orientation.
evidence: This is supported by EPR depth measurement data.

claim: The presence of PtdIns(4,5)P2 promotes a tilt of the C2B domain.
source: The presence of PtdIns(4,5)P2 is found to promote a tilt of the C2B domain, which is consistent with its interaction with the polybasic face.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the EPR depth data and modeling.

claim: PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 play a synergistic role in the binding of syt-1 to the membrane.
source: Together with the stopped-flow measurements described above, these data indicate that PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 play a synergistic role in the binding of syt-1 to the membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental approaches.

claim: When both PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 are present, the Ca2+-binding loops of syt-1 penetrate deeper into the bilayer than they do when the membrane contains PtdIns(4,5)P2 alone.
source: When both PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 are present, the Ca2+-binding loops of syt-1 penetrate deeper into the bilayer than they do when the membrane contains PtdIns(4,5)P2 alone, leading to a tighter binding of the C2AB fragment to the membrane, which is reflected by a decrease in the dissociation rate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from EPR and kinetic data.

claim: Deeper penetration leads to a tighter binding of the C2AB fragment to the membrane, which is reflected by a decrease in the dissociation rate.
source: When both PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 are present, the Ca2+-binding loops of syt-1 penetrate deeper into the bilayer than they do when the membrane contains PtdIns(4,5)P2 alone, leading to a tighter binding of the C2AB fragment to the membrane, which is reflected by a decrease in the dissociation rate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from EPR and kinetic data.

claim: Only small changes in the binding enthalpy were observed upon injection of O-PSer into a solution containing the C2AB fragment.
source: In our experiments, only small changes in the binding enthalpy were observed upon injection of O-PSer into a solution containing the C2AB fragment, precluding a quantitative assessment of the thermodynamics of binding.
evidence: This is a direct observation from ITC experiments.

claim: Binding of InsP3 to the C2AB fragment was highly exothermic, showing a stoichiometry of 1:1 and an affinity of 14 ± 2 µM.
source: By contrast, binding of InsP3 to the C2AB fragment was highly exothermic, showing a stoichiometry of 1:1 and an affinity of 14 ± 2 µM (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Addition of O-PSer to the C2AB fragment did not induce significant changes in the chemical shifts.
source: In agreement with the lack of enthalpy changes, addition of O-PSer to the C2AB fragment did not induce significant changes in the chemical shifts (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by NMR experimental data.

claim: The addition of InsP3 induced chemical shift changes primarily in the polybasic lysine patch of the C2B domain.
source: By contrast, the addition of InsP3 induced chemical shift changes primarily in the polybasic lysine patch of the C2B domain, with the highest chemical shifts observable for residues K325, K326 and K327, confirming previous reports which established the polybasic lysine patch of the C2B domain as the primary binding site of PtdIns(4,5)P2 (Vrljic et al., 2011; Li et al., 2006; Bai et al., 2004; van den Bogaart et al., 2012) (Figure 3b,c and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by NMR experimental data shown in Figure 3b,c.

claim: Residues K325, K326 and K327 show the highest chemical shifts upon InsP3 addition.
source: By contrast, the addition of InsP3 induced chemical shift changes primarily in the polybasic lysine patch of the C2B domain, with the highest chemical shifts observable for residues K325, K326 and K327, confirming previous reports which established the polybasic lysine patch of the C2B domain as the primary binding site of PtdIns(4,5)P2 (Vrljic et al., 2011; Li et al., 2006; Bai et al., 2004; van den Bogaart et al., 2012) (Figure 3b,c and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by NMR experimental data.

claim: Residues located in the Ca2+-binding sites of the C2A and C2B domains exhibited significant but smaller chemical shift changes upon InsP3 addition.
source: In addition to the polybasic lysine patch, residues located in the Ca2+-binding sites of the C2A and C2B domains exhibited significant but smaller chemical shift changes (Figure 3b,c).
evidence: This is supported by NMR experimental data shown in Figure 3b,c.

claim: In the absence of Ca2+, the binding affinity of the wild-type protein was significantly lower than in the presence of Ca2+.
source: In the absence of Ca2+, the binding affinity of the wild-type protein was significantly lower than in the presence of Ca2+.
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data comparing Ca2+ conditions.

claim: The reduction in binding affinity in the absence of Ca2+ is mediated by the Ca2+-binding site of the C2B domain.
source: This reduction is mediated by the Ca2+-binding site of the C2B domain: it was abolished in the C2Ab and C2ab mutants but not in the C2aB mutant (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data with mutants shown in Figure 4d.

claim: The negatively charged side chains in the Ca2+-binding site reduce the affinity of the negatively charged InsP3 through unfavorable Coulombic interactions.
source: Apparently, the negatively charged side chains in the Ca2+-binding site reduce the affinity of the negatively charged InsP3 through unfavorable Coulombic interactions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mutant data.

claim: Neutralizing negative charges by Ca2+-binding or by deletion through mutagenesis are equally effective in preventing the thermodynamic penalty resulting from repulsive interactions.
source: Neutralizing these charges by Ca2+-binding or, alternatively, by their deletion by mutagenesis are equally effective in preventing the thermodynamic penalty resulting from repulsive interactions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mutant data.

claim: The lower affinities in the absence of Ca2+ were mainly due to a decrease in binding enthalpy rather than to reduced entropy.
source: In line with that proposition, the lower affinities were mainly due to a decrease in binding enthalpy rather than to reduced entropy (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; Figure 4—figure supplement 2), as one would expect for a primarily electrostatic effect.
evidence: This is supported by thermodynamic data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: No change of the binding stoichiometry was observed in any of the different conditions and mutants tested.
source: Nevertheless, no change of the binding stoichiometry was observed in any of the different conditions and mutants tested (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The C2B domain bound InsP3 in a manner similar to the C2AB fragment.
source: As expected, the C2B domain bound InsP3 in a manner similar to the C2AB fragment.
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data.

claim: Binding of InsP3 to the C2A domain yielded only small enthalpy changes.
source: By contrast, binding of InsP3 to the C2A domain yielded only small enthalpy changes, confirming that C2B is indeed the domain responsible for InsP3 binding (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: The presence or absence of SNARE-complex made no difference to InsP3 binding to the isolated C2B domain.
source: The presence or absence of SNARE-complex made no difference to InsP3 binding to the isolated C2B domain (Figure 4f), in agreement with previous observations from our group (Park et al., 2015) .
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 4f and previous citations.

claim: Under physiological conditions, the C2AB fragment binds preferentially to PtdIns(4,5)P2.
source: This evidence suggests that, under physiological conditions, the C2AB fragment binds preferentially to PtdIns(4,5)P2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from ITC experiments with SNARE complex.

claim: The presence of the SNARE complex resulted in a moderate decrease in affinity of InsP3 to the C2AB fragment.
source: Interestingly, the presence of the SNARE complex resulted in a moderate decrease in affinity of InsP3 to the C2AB fragment, in contrast to above results using the C2B domain (Figure 4g,i).
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 4g,i.

claim: The SNARE complex binds the C2AB fragment with higher affinity than it does the C2B domain.
source: Our results show that the SNARE complex binds the C2AB fragment with higher affinity than it does the C2B domain, and that K326 and K327 play an important role in this binding (Figure 4h,i), in agreement with recent findings (Brewer et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 4h,i and previous citations.

claim: K326 and K327 play an important role in SNARE complex binding.
source: Our results show that the SNARE complex binds the C2AB fragment with higher affinity than it does the C2B domain, and that K326 and K327 play an important role in this binding (Figure 4h,i), in agreement with recent findings (Brewer et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 4h,i and previous citations.

claim: In the absence of Ca2+, binding of InsP3 to the KAKA mutant was abolished.
source: In the absence of Ca2+, binding to InsP3 was abolished (Figure 4b), as previously reported (van den Bogaart et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 4b and previous citations.

claim: In the presence of Ca2+, the KAKA mutant was able to bind to InsP3, but with lower affinity than the wild-type C2AB fragment.
source: However, in the presence of Ca2+, the KAKA mutant was able to bind to InsP3, but with lower affinity than the wild-type C2AB fragment (Figure 4a,d).
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 4a,d.

claim: The KAKA mutant was found to bind with reduced affinity to either PtdSer- or PtdIns(4,5)P2-containing bilayers in the presence of Ca2+.
source: Using sedimentation, the KAKA mutant was found to bind with reduced affinity to either PtdSer- or PtdIns(4,5)P2-containing bilayers in the presence of Ca2+ (Figure 5a,b,c and Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by vesicle sedimentation assay data shown in Figure 5 and Table 2.

claim: The KAKA mutation produced only a small effect on the binding to PtdSer-containing bilayers.
source: Remarkably, the KAKA mutation produced only a small effect on the binding to PtdSer-containing bilayers (Figure 5a), but dramatically reduced the membrane affinity of C2AB fragment to 2% PtdIns(4,5)P2 bilayers (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by vesicle sedimentation assay data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The KAKA mutation dramatically reduced the membrane affinity of C2AB fragment to 2% PtdIns(4,5)P2 bilayers.
source: Remarkably, the KAKA mutation produced only a small effect on the binding to PtdSer-containing bilayers (Figure 5a), but dramatically reduced the membrane affinity of C2AB fragment to 2% PtdIns(4,5)P2 bilayers (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by vesicle sedimentation assay data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: In 2% PtdIns(4,5)P2 membranes, the KAKA mutant altered the membrane-binding free energy of C2AB fragment by 7.5 kJ/mole.
source: In these membranes, the KAKA mutant altered the membrane-binding free energy of C2AB fragment by 7.5 kJ/mole.
evidence: This is a calculated value from the experimental data.

claim: In the absence of Ca2+, the KAKA mutant failed to bind to PtdSer- or PtdIns(4,5)P2-containing bilayers.
source: In the absence of Ca2+, the KAKA mutant failed to bind to PtdSer- or PtdIns(4,5)P2-containing bilayers (Figure 5d,e).
evidence: This is supported by vesicle sedimentation assay data shown in Figure 5d,e.

claim: In the absence of Ca2+, the KAKA mutant did bind to membranes composed of both PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2.
source: However, this variant did bind to membranes composed of both PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 (Figure 5f), indicating a synergistic activity of PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 towards syt-1 C2AB fragment binding.
evidence: This is supported by vesicle sedimentation assay data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: The affinity between the C2AB fragment and membranes containing both PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 in the absence of Ca2+ indicates that at an accessible lipid concentration of 20 µM, 50% of the protein is bound.
source: The affinity between the C2AB fragment and membranes containing both PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 (Table 3) in the absence of Ca2+ indicates that at an accessible lipid concentration of 20 µM, 50% of the protein is bound.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the partition coefficient data in Table 3.

claim: In full-length syt-1, the C2 domains are tethered near the membrane interface and thus experience a very high local lipid concentration.
source: However, in full-length syt-1, the C2 domains are tethered near the membrane interface and thus experience a very high local lipid concentration.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the physiological context.

claim: Assuming the domains lie within 4 nm of the interface, the effective membrane concentration seen by the C2 domains will be well over four orders of magnitude higher than 20 µM.
source: Assuming the domains lie within 4 nm of the interface, the effective membrane concentration seen by the C2 domains will be well over four orders of magnitude higher than 20 µM.
evidence: This is a calculation based on geometric considerations.

claim: The high local concentration represents a shift in the binding free energy to favor membrane association by about 25 kJ/mole.
source: This represents a shift in the binding free energy to favor membrane association by about 25 kJ/mole, may be even higher when considering that syntaxin and PtdIns(4,5)P2 form clusters that increase the local concentration of PtdIns(4,5)P2 in the plasma membrane (Honigmann et al., 2013; van den Bogaart et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a calculation based on thermodynamic principles and previous citations.

claim: The affinity of C2AB fragment to membranes containing PtdIns(4,5)P2 and PtdSer is significant even in the absence of Ca2+.
source: We conclude that the affinity of C2AB fragment to membranes containing PtdIns(4,5)P2 and PtdSer is significant even in the absence of Ca2+ (Table 3).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the partition coefficient data in Table 3.

claim: PtdIns(4,5)P2 primarily binds to the polybasic lysine patch of the C2B domain, which includes two Lys residues (K326 and K327).
source: Taken together, our results demonstrate that PtdIns(4,5)P2 primarily binds to the polybasic lysine patch of the C2B domain, which includes two Lys residues (K326 and K327), rather than to the Ca2+-binding sites of C2B domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental approaches.

claim: PtdIns(4,5)P2 does not bind to the Ca2+-binding sites of C2B domain.
source: Taken together, our results demonstrate that PtdIns(4,5)P2 primarily binds to the polybasic lysine patch of the C2B domain, which includes two Lys residues (K326 and K327), rather than to the Ca2+-binding sites of C2B domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental approaches.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 is the likely target of the polybasic patch of the C2B domain.
source: As discussed below, the relative affinity of the C2AB fragment for PtdIns(4,5)P2 versus its affinity for the SNAREs suggests that PI(4,5)P2 is the likely target of the polybasic patch of the C2B domain, in agreement with recent reports (Wang, 2016; Park et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from affinity comparisons and previous citations.

claim: Ca2+ increases C2B's affinity for PtdIns(4,5)P2 by neutralizing the negatively charged side chain at the Ca2+-binding site of the C2B domain.
source: Furthermore, Ca2+ increases C2B's affinity for PtdIns(4,5)P2, probably by neutralizing the negatively charged side chain at the Ca2+-binding site of the C2B domain, allowing a tighter binding of the polybasic patch to PtdIns(4,5)P2.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Phosphorylated phosphatidylinositides increased the apparent affinities of syt-1 C2AB fragment to membranes.
source: Phosphorylated phosphatidylinositides increased the apparent affinities (Figure 6a), with the bimolecular association (kon) and the unimolecular dissociation rate (koff) constants being enhanced and reduced, respectively (Figure 6b,c).
evidence: This is supported by stopped-flow experimental data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The 5–10-fold decrease in koff and Kd was progressively higher in the presence of bisphosphorylated phosphatidylinositols (PtdInsP2) and triphosphorylated phosphatidylinositols (PtdInsP3) than in the presence of monophosphorylated phosphatidylinositols (PtdInsP).
source: The 5–10-fold decrease in koff and Kd (koff/kon) was progressively higher in the presence of bisphosphorylated phosphatidylinositols (PtdInsP2) and triphosphorylated phosphatidylinositols (PtdInsP3) than in the presence of monophosphorylated phosphatidylinositols (PtdInsP) (Figure 6a,c).
evidence: This is supported by stopped-flow experimental data shown in Figure 6a,c.

claim: PtdInsP2 or PtdInsP3 increased the association rate constant moderately by 2–3-fold.
source: While PtdInsP2 or PtdInsP3 increased the association rate constant moderately by 2–3-fold, PtdInsP or phosphatidylinositols (PtdIns) had no measurable effect on the binding kinetics (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is supported by stopped-flow experimental data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: PtdInsP or phosphatidylinositols (PtdIns) had no measurable effect on the binding kinetics.
source: While PtdInsP2 or PtdInsP3 increased the association rate constant moderately by 2–3-fold, PtdInsP or phosphatidylinositols (PtdIns) had no measurable effect on the binding kinetics (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is supported by stopped-flow experimental data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Syt-1 does not discriminate between the different tested phosphorylated phosphatidylinositol stereoisomers.
source: Thus, these results suggest that syt-1 does not discriminate between the different tested phosphorylated phosphatidylinositol stereoisomers, and that the increase in affinity is mainly due to the higher charge density of the different PtdInsPx species.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the stopped-flow data.

claim: The increase in affinity is mainly due to the higher charge density of the different PtdInsPx species.
source: Thus, these results suggest that syt-1 does not discriminate between the different tested phosphorylated phosphatidylinositol stereoisomers, and that the increase in affinity is mainly due to the higher charge density of the different PtdInsPx species.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the stopped-flow data.

claim: Ins(1,3,5)P3 showed lower affinity than the other tested stereoisomers.
source: Surprisingly, Ins(1,3,5)P3 showed lower affinity than the other tested stereoisomers (Figure 6e) because of a less favorable binding enthalpy (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by ITC experimental data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: The estimated bimolecular association rate constants (kon) showed minor differences at different Ca2+ concentrations (50, 100, 500 and 1000 µM).
source: Nevertheless, for all other tested concentrations, the estimated bimolecular association rate constants (kon) showed minor differences (Figure 6g), meaning that the increase in the Ca2+concentration did not drive the C2AB fragment to the membrane faster, at least not in this concentration regime.
evidence: This is supported by stopped-flow experimental data shown in Figure 6g.

claim: The increase in the Ca2+ concentration did not drive the C2AB fragment to the membrane faster.
source: Nevertheless, for all other tested concentrations, the estimated bimolecular association rate constants (kon) showed minor differences (Figure 6g), meaning that the increase in the Ca2+concentration did not drive the C2AB fragment to the membrane faster, at least not in this concentration regime.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the stopped-flow data.

claim: The dissociation rate constant (koff) showed a substantial decrease at Ca2+ concentrations over 50 µM.
source: In contrast, the dissociation rate constant (koff) showed a substantial decrease at concentrations over 50 µM (Figure 6h) with no further decrease at Ca2+ > 100 µM.
evidence: This is supported by stopped-flow experimental data shown in Figure 6h.

claim: There was no further decrease in koff at Ca2+ > 100 µM.
source: In contrast, the dissociation rate constant (koff) showed a substantial decrease at concentrations over 50 µM (Figure 6h) with no further decrease at Ca2+ > 100 µM.
evidence: This is supported by stopped-flow experimental data shown in Figure 6h.

claim: The dissociation constant (Kd) followed a similar trend to the unimolecular dissociation rate constant (koff).
source: Because of this, the dissociation constant (Kd), followed a similar trend to the unimolecular dissociation rate constant (koff) (Figure 6f,h).
evidence: This is supported by stopped-flow experimental data shown in Figure 6f,h.

claim: The association rate of the C2AB fragment is largely Ca2+-independent.
source: In summary, these results suggest that the association rate of the C2AB fragment is largely Ca2+-independent.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the stopped-flow data at different Ca2+ concentrations.

claim: The increased membrane affinity of the C2AB fragment in the presence of Ca2+ is due to a decreased dissociation rate from the membrane.
source: The increased membrane affinity of the C2AB fragment in the presence of Ca2+ is due to a decreased dissociation rate from the membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the stopped-flow data at different Ca2+ concentrations.

claim: Ca2+ lengthens the period during which syt-1 remains bound once membrane binding has occurred.
source: As a result, Ca2+ lengthens the period during which syt-1 remains bound once membrane binding has occurred.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetic data.

claim: PtdSer and PtdIns(4,5)P2 act synergistically to promote deeper penetration of the Ca2+-binding site of the C2B domain into the membrane.
